questions.question: Which purchase in 1803 greatly enlarged U.S. territory?
choices: Gadsden Purchase
Alaska Purchase
Florida Purchase
Louisiana Purchase

questions.question: Who explored parts of the Louisiana Purchase and the Pacific Northwest for the U.S. government?
choices: Lewis and Clark
Marquette and Joliet
Hernán Cortés and Francisco Pizarro
John Cabot and Henry Hudson

questions.question: What was the Oregon Trail?
choices: A canal between the Atlantic and Great Lakes
A railway crossing only the Deep South
An overland migration route to the Pacific Northwest
A sea route connecting California and China

questions.question: Which event drew large numbers of migrants to California beginning in 1849?
choices: Completion of the Panama Canal
Gold Rush
Opening of Ellis Island
Ratification of the Monroe Doctrine

questions.question: Which act offered eligible settlers public land subject to residency and improvement requirements?
choices: Homestead Act
Dawes Act
Morrill Tariff
Pendleton Act

questions.question: Where was the first transcontinental railroad joined in 1869?
choices: St. Louis, Missouri
Santa Fe, New Mexico
Portland, Oregon
Promontory Summit, Utah

questions.question: Which treaty ended the Mexican-American War and transferred extensive territory to the United States?
choices: Treaty of Ghent
Treaty of Paris of 1783
Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
Webster-Ashburton Treaty

questions.question: Why did settlers move west for reasons beyond gold?
choices: Every migrant was required to work in a gold mine
Land, work, religious goals, and other opportunities attracted migrants
Western migration occurred only through military orders
Only wealthy merchants could legally move west

questions.question: How did federal land policies encourage settlement?
choices: They offered ways to acquire land claimed as public domain
They prohibited farms beyond the Mississippi
They required settlers to buy land only from European monarchs
They guaranteed profitable harvests to every claimant

questions.question: Why is describing western land as simply empty inaccurate?
choices: The West contained no land suitable for settlement
All land had already been purchased privately from Spain
Only coastal regions had any human settlement
Indigenous peoples already lived on and used these lands

questions.question: How did railroads affect western economies?
choices: They ended trade between the West and eastern cities
They made every western business locally self-sufficient
They connected farms, mines, and towns to wider markets
They removed the need to transport agricultural products

questions.question: Why did the expansion of slavery become a major political issue?
choices: Every territory had already banned slavery permanently
New territories raised disputes about slavery's legal status
The Constitution required slavery in all western states
Slavery affected only international diplomacy

questions.question: How did the Indian Removal Act contribute to expansion?
choices: It supported forced displacement of Indigenous communities from eastern lands
It protected every Indigenous community from relocation
It granted all tribes voting seats in Congress
It ended settler demand for farmland

questions.question: Why could homesteading be difficult despite inexpensive land?
choices: Claimants were forbidden from cultivating crops
The government provided no legal route to ownership
Every homestead was located within an existing city
Settlers still faced equipment costs, harsh conditions, and uncertain harvests

questions.question: How did Chinese immigrants contribute to western development?
choices: They served only as federal land surveyors
They were the sole group permitted to own western land
Many worked in mining, businesses, and railroad construction
They held every railroad executive position

questions.question: Which sequence orders these expansion events correctly?
choices: Gold Rush, Louisiana Purchase, railroad completion
Louisiana Purchase, California Gold Rush, completion of the transcontinental railroad
Railroad completion, Gold Rush, Louisiana Purchase
Louisiana Purchase, railroad completion, Gold Rush

questions.question: A historian compares settler land claims with Indigenous treaty records. What issue is central?
choices: Competing claims and dispossession during expansion
The independence of European colonies in Africa
The creation of the Federal Reserve
The rise of automobile suburbs after World War II

questions.question: Which evidence best evaluates railroads' economic impact?
choices: Only the names of locomotives
Only a list of presidential birthdays
Only the design of state flags
Changes in shipping costs, market access, and settlement patterns

questions.question: Which comparison of western experiences is accurate?
choices: Every group gained equal control of land and government
Only farmers were affected by railroad development
Settlers, Indigenous peoples, and immigrant workers often experienced expansion differently
Every migrant moved west for the same reason

questions.question: Why should a history of expansion examine both opportunities and costs?
choices: Economic growth made all treaties unnecessary
Territorial and economic growth also involved displacement and conflict
New states formed without political disputes
Expansion affected land size but not people's lives
